learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Entry checks are low stakes; an unresolved fresh re-entry returns control without exit credit.

items.title: Starting check: choose the system
items.prompt: A sealed metal bottle of water cools on a bench. The analysis defines the water as the system. Which statement follows from that boundary choice?
options: The room is part of the system because it exchanges energy.
Matter must leave the water whenever heat leaves it.
The water cannot change temperature because the bottle is sealed.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: apply the Zeroth Law
items.prompt: Object A is in thermal equilibrium with thermometer B. Object C later reaches thermal equilibrium with B at the same reading. What can be concluded?
options: A and C contain equal total internal energy.
A and C must have equal masses.
Heat must continuously flow from A to C.
A and C have equal temperatures.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: classify the quantity
items.prompt: A gas follows two different processes between identical initial and final states. Which quantity must be identical for both processes?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: compare paths
items.prompt: Process X and Process Y begin and end at the same thermodynamic states. X transfers more heat into the system than Y. What must differ?
options: The work transfer differs between X and Y.
The Zeroth Law becomes invalid for one path.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: thermal-equilibrium limit
items.prompt: Two copper blocks are in thermal equilibrium but have different masses. Which property is necessarily equal?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: endpoint versus process data
items.prompt: A state table shows identical initial and final pressure, volume, and temperature for two paths. A process log reports different heat transfers. Which statement is consistent?
options: Different heat proves the final states are different.
Same endpoints require equal heat and equal work separately.
Internal energy is undefined unless the path is known.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: use the endpoint test
items.prompt: Which question best identifies whether a thermodynamic quantity is a state function?
options: Was the quantity measured with a thermometer?
Did energy cross the boundary during the process?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: identify path dependence
items.prompt: A liquid reaches the same final state by direct heating or by compression followed by cooling. Which reported quantity may differ between routes?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: translate equilibrium statements
items.prompt: If TA = TB and TB = TC, what is the valid Zeroth-Law conclusion?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: compare two sensors
items.prompt: Sensor X equilibrates with bath P at 310 K. Sensor Y equilibrates with bath P and also reads 310 K. What follows about X and Y after equilibration?
options: They store the same internal energy.
They absorbed the same amount of heat.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: work sign
items.prompt: Using ΔU = q + w with w defined as work done on the system, a gas expands and pushes the surroundings. What is the sign of w?
options: Undefined even after the convention is stated
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: close the ledger
items.prompt: A system absorbs 150 J of heat while doing 40 J of work on the surroundings. Under ΔU = q + w, what is ΔU?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: rectangular PV area
items.prompt: A gas expands at 200 kPa from 1.0 L to 2.5 L. What is the work done by the gas?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: compression work
items.prompt: A gas is compressed at 150 kPa from 4.0 L to 2.0 L. Under the work-on-system convention, what is w?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: combine heat and PV work
items.prompt: A gas absorbs 450 J while expanding at constant pressure and doing 180 J of work on the surroundings. What is its internal-energy change?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: read a rectangular cycle
items.prompt: A gas traces a clockwise rectangle from 2 L to 5 L between pressures of 100 and 300 kPa. What is the net work done by the gas per cycle?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: translate transfer language
items.prompt: Under ΔU = q + w, which translation is correct?
options: Heat leaves: q > 0; surroundings compress system: w < 0
Heat leaves: q < 0; system expands: w > 0
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: new energy ledger
items.prompt: A system releases 90 J of heat while 140 J of work is done on it. What is ΔU under the stated convention?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: cycle area and direction
items.prompt: Which rule correctly interprets a simple closed PV loop?
options: The final volume alone gives all cyclic work.
Only the highest pressure determines net work.
Clockwise and counterclockwise loops have identical work direction.
Area gives magnitude; direction gives sign.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: reverse the loop
items.prompt: A counterclockwise rectangular PV cycle encloses 250 J. Under the work-on-system convention, what is net w?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: phase entropy
items.prompt: For the same pure substance under comparable conditions, which ordering generally has increasing entropy?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: add both columns
items.prompt: A process has ΔSsystem = −12 J/K and ΔSsurroundings = +20 J/K. What is ΔSuniverse for the stated direction?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: assign a phase-change sign
items.prompt: A pure liquid vaporizes. What is the expected sign of the system entropy change?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: apply the Second Law
items.prompt: For a proposed direction, ΔSsystem = +6 J/K and ΔSsurroundings = −2 J/K. Which conclusion follows?
options: The direction is impossible because surroundings entropy decreases.
The system is at equilibrium because one term is negative.
The reverse direction is spontaneous under the same conditions.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: system decrease
items.prompt: During condensation, the system entropy falls by 18 J/K and the surroundings entropy rises by 27 J/K. What is the correct judgment?
options: Condensation is forbidden because system entropy decreases.
The system is at equilibrium because both terms are nonzero.
Vaporization and condensation are equally favored.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: interpret an entropy table
items.prompt: A table lists three proposed directions: P has ΔSsystem = +5 and ΔSsurroundings = −5; Q has −4 and +9; R has +7 and −10 J/K. Which direction is spontaneous?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: phase order before direction
items.prompt: Which change normally lowers the system entropy for a pure substance?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: sublimation sign
items.prompt: A solid sublimes directly to a gas. What is the expected sign of ΔSsystem?
options: Positive only if surroundings entropy is zero
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: use the total
items.prompt: Which expression is the Second-Law direction test for a process and its surroundings?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: new entropy ledger
items.prompt: A phase change has ΔSsystem = +14 J/K and ΔSsurroundings = −19 J/K. What follows for the stated direction?
options: It is spontaneous because system entropy rises.
It is at equilibrium because the signs differ.
It is spontaneous because entropy magnitudes must be added.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: transfer mechanism
items.prompt: Energy from the Sun reaches a spacecraft across nearly empty space. Which transfer mechanism carries that energy?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: use specific heat
items.prompt: How much heat is required to warm 50 g of a material with c = 4 J/(g·K) by 3 K, with no phase change?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: compare specific heat
items.prompt: Equal masses of materials A and B receive equal heat. A changes temperature less than B. Which conclusion follows?
options: A has the smaller specific heat.
Both must have equal specific heat.
Specific heat cannot affect temperature change.
A has the greater specific heat.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: thermal expansion
items.prompt: A uniform metal rod is heated while remaining in one phase and unconstrained. What change is normally expected?
options: Its mass increases because heat is matter.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: isolated mixing
items.prompt: In an insulated cup, a hot object loses 900 J before both objects reach one final temperature. How much heat does the cooler object gain?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: follow a phase-diagram path
items.prompt: A constant-pressure path moves from the liquid region across the liquid–gas boundary into the gas region while energy is added. What occurs at the boundary in the ideal model?
options: The liquid cools through the boundary with no energy transfer.
Only thermal expansion occurs and phase remains liquid.
Temperature rises continuously during the entire phase conversion.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: signed calorimetry
items.prompt: Which equation correctly represents two objects exchanging heat in an insulated container?
options: q1 = q2 with both signs positive
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: new heat balance
items.prompt: In an insulated container, sample X gains 350 J while reaching equilibrium. What is the signed heat change of sample Y?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: choose the phase equation
items.prompt: During an ideal heating-curve plateau while melting continues, which equation accounts for added heat?
options: q = mcΔT with a large ΔT
q = PΔV only for every melting process
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: cross a different boundary
items.prompt: At constant pressure, a path moves from the solid region across the solid–liquid boundary while heat is added. Which description is correct at the boundary?
options: Freezing releases latent heat while the solid fraction grows.
Latent heat melts at fixed temperature.
Convection converts the solid with no phase energy.
The sample remains entirely solid after entering the liquid region.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.
